short: Synthetic EMG with confidence filtering (M03, standard) gives a small real-EMG gain, 23.30% to 21.87% WER on one speaker; large gains appear only on synthetic test EMG.
position: The paper changes training data (M03): EMG generated from LibriSpeech audio by a speech-to-EMG generator, filtered by phoneme loss and mixed 1:1 by utterance count with real voiced EMG. The design is standard: a speech-driven generator is the usual approach among 13 ledger studies on synthetic training signals, and lip reading scaled it earlier. The real-EMG gain is small, 23.30% to 21.87% WER on one voiced speaker, from single values without spread, against a baseline value reported by earlier work and not stated as re-run. The large gains, 37.63% to 8.75%, are on synthetic EMG from the same generator and show agreement with it, not robustness. Speaker independence, silent EMG and clinical use are not tested.
